item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian warship off Libya's coast
item.description:
Kyiv, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was behind an attack on a Russian warship off Libya on Sunday, claiming Ukrainian naval drones sank the vessel. It marked the latest attack in the North African nation tied to the Russia-Ukraine war.
Zelenskyy said Monday in a social media post that Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones in the operation, which sank a Russian corvette. The Ukrainian leader described the ship as one of Russia's newest vessels commissioned in 2023 during Russia's invasion.
"Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk," he wrote. He added that a Ka-27 military helicopter was destroyed in the attack.
A satellite image shows a capsized Russian corvette and the northern area of the port after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, which Libya's eastern-based government said was caused by a suspected drone attack, in Benghazi, Libya, on Nov. 22, 2026. The vessel later sank, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
Vantor / Handout via REUTERS
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.
Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara off Libya on Sunday. Zelenskyy said Moscow had used the vessel to transport weapons. The Angara has been under U.S. and international sanctions for illegally transporting weapons for Russia.

item.title: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by "all available means"
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran said Monday it would use "all available means" to counter the U.S. naval blockade of the country's ports, which a foreign ministry official described as "an act of military aggression" against the country.President Trump said in a social media post Sunday that Iran had "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time" during the nearly nine-month war, but that the increasing attacks had "done no damage." A media outlet linked to Iran's Houthi allies said Monday that a Saudi attack on Yemen's port city of Hodeida killed 17 people and wounded 11, as fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis continues to intensify.
New Updates
5:19 PM / November 23, 2026
3 oil tankers struck naval mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy says
The Iranian navy said in a statement carried on state media that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, resulting in "explosions and massive fires."
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
Iranian forces have been attacking shipping through the strait in a campaign aimed at hiking global energy prices to pressure the United States, which has imposed a crippling blockade on Iranian ports.
On Saturday, three other oil tankers were hit in what appeared to be the latest Iranian strikes on shipping through the strategic chokepoint.
CBS/AP

item.title: U.S. man convicted of killing U.K. woman he met on fetish website
item.description:
A Florida man was convicted by a U.S. jury on Friday of the 2025 murder of a British woman he met on a fetish website.
Dwain Hall, 54, was found guilty of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby, and was sentenced to two consecutive life terms, Florida prosecutors said in a statement.
"This was an extraordinary and deeply disturbing case involving circumstances that are difficult to comprehend," said Bill Gladson, state attorney for the Fifth Judicial Circuit.
According to prosecutors, Hall and the 32-year-old Exelby had communicated for about two years using a fetish website called "Motherless.com" and an encrypted application called Sessions.
The now-defunct Motherless features "content that depicted various fetishes, including extreme BDSM, torture, and rape material," according to court documents.
During their exchanges, Exelby, who reportedly struggled with mental health issues, allegedly expressed a desire to be murdered.
A GoFundMe set up on behalf of her family has raised more than $12,000.
"Sonia struggled with her mental health, and she knew from her own experiences how difficult life could sometimes be," the GoFundMe says. "But Sonia was passionate about using the challenges and experiences she had faced to help others."

item.title: U.S. will host the 2031 Women's World Cup, FIFA announces
item.description:
The United States will host another World Cup, as FIFA confirmed Monday that the country will lead a regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women's World Cup. The co-hosting group includes Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while a different U.K. project, led by England, was ratified for the 2035 edition. It will be England's first time hosting the games since 1966.
The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments — the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games — and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.
"This will be the largest women's sporting event in history," the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body's headquarters in Zurich. "Which means we have to deliver."
FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup, which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.
The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.
Atlanta, which hosted men's World Cup games this year, is among the U.S. cities included in the U.S.-Mexico-Costa Rica-Jamaica proposal for 2031, CBS News Atlanta reported. The station cited a report released by FIFA earlier this month, which gave the proposal a score of 4.4 out of 5 and noted that the bid "exceeded the minimum hosting requirements in the FIFA Women's World Cup 2031 technical evaluation."
The U.S. bid also proposed stadiums in Charlotte, Dallas, Denver, Houston, Kansas City, Los Angeles, Minneapolis and Nashville, in addition to MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where the men's final took place in July.

item.title: Capture of drug lord on FBI's most wanted list leads to more arrests
item.description:
Eight suspected members of a gang led by Fausto Isidro Meza Flores have been arrested, Mexico's defense ministry said Sunday, after widespread violence swept across Sinaloa following the drug kingpin's capture.
Meza Flores, alias "Chapo Isidro," was captured on Friday in the northwestern state during a special forces raid in coordination with U.S. intelligence.
The military operation sparked panic in Guasave, sending civilians fleeing from erupting gunfire. Elsewhere in the state, suspected gang members reportedly erected improvised roadblocks.
In clashes with security forces, 16 cartel suspects have been killed since the operation began, Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla said Monday. Four soldiers also died.
The fresh arrests took place during a patrol by special forces who "were fired upon by members of a criminal group" linked to Chapo Isidro, Mexico's defense ministry posted on X. The ministry included a short video showing special forces arresting suspects at night.
"In repelling the attack, they arrested eight members of the 'Beltran Leyva' criminal organization ... including one minor, who had participated in the roadblocks on November 20," the ministry's post said.
The military also seized several high-caliber weapons and six vehicles, two of which had "improvised armor and a turret for mounting machine guns."
Chapo Isidro, 44, led a drug trafficking organization affiliated with the Beltran Leyva gang and allied with one of two rival factions of the powerful Sinaloa cartel, according to U.S. and Mexican authorities.

item.title: Why some Europeans have started prepping for doomsday
item.description:
European governments are increasingly urging citizens to prepare for up to 72 hours without access to food, water, electricity or communications.
France, the United Kingdom, Ireland and the Netherlands have all launched campaigns encouraging households to take steps to prepare for events caused by anything from extreme weather to cyberattacks that could disrupt digital networks or critical supply chains.
Last month, major French supermarket chains were hit by a cyberattack that caused the temperature in thousands of refrigerator and freezer units to soar, wasting tens of thousands of pounds of food and stoking concerns about food security.
French officials later accused a cyber unit of Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of being behind the attack, which was mirrored several weeks later by a nearly identical cyberattack targeting grocery stores in several other European nations. Belgian authorities blamed that, too, on Iran.
Europe was also hit by a record-setting, continent-wide heatwave last summer, triggering wildfires and severe drought even in areas such as northern England, where sustained, excess heat and a lack of precipitation have long been rare exceptions, not the rule.
The European governments have recommended that citizens buy and store emergency supplies including bottled water and canned foods to last households up to three days, along with AM/FM radios and sleeping bags.
Cans of beans and other long-life foods are seen in a shopping trolley, Nov. 10, 2026, in Northwich, England.
Christopher Furlong/Getty
CBS News spoke with residents and tourists on the streets of London to see who, if anyone, was taking the advice to heart.
